name: Purchase Approval - Spend Limit, Department and Vendor Risk

parameters.content:
## Purchase Approval by Spend Limit, Department and Vendor Risk

### How it works

A purchase request is evaluated against policy and routed to exactly the approvals it needs.

- **Spend limits:** tiers decide the approval levels (default: up to 500 USD auto-approve, up to 5k manager, up to 25k manager + finance, above that manager + finance + CFO). Spend with the same vendor in the last 30 days is added, so splitting an order does not avoid a tier.
- **Department:** unknown or frozen departments are rejected. Requests that exceed the remaining department budget add finance. If the requester is the department manager, finance approves instead (no self-approval).
- **Vendor risk:** blocked vendors are rejected. Unknown or unapproved vendors need procurement. High risk adds procurement and security review and is never auto-approved. Medium risk adds procurement above a threshold.

Approvers get an email with approve / reject links and decide one level at a time. No answer means a reminder (default every 24h, twice), then the request expires. Every step is audited. Approved requests get a PO number and the amount is committed to the department budget.

### Setup steps

- Add Postgres and SMTP (email) credentials, then run the manual setup once.
- Edit **Set Approval Policy**: spend tiers, approver emails, thresholds, currency rates, reminders, sender email, Slack webhook.
- Replace the demo vendors and departments with your own data.
- Activate the workflow (the approval links need an active workflow and a reachable n8n URL), then test with `POST /purchase-request`:
  `{"requesterEmail":"a@b.com","department":"engineering","vendorId":"cloudco","amount":8000,"currency":"USD","description":"Annual licence"}`

### Layout

1 Setup
2-5 Intake, policy, routing, finalize
6 Approval chain

## 1. One-time setup

Run manually once. Creates vendors (with risk level), departments (budget, manager), requests and audit log tables, plus demo vendors and departments to test every rule.

## 2. Intake & validation

`POST /purchase-request` with requesterEmail, department, vendorId, amount, currency and description. Input is validated and converted to USD.

## 4. Acknowledge & route

Answers the requester immediately, then routes: auto-approve, send for approval, or reject.

## 5. Finalize, notify & audit

Commits the decision: PO number and budget commitment on approval, audit log entry, then email to the requester and a Slack audit message. Policy decisions and chain results both end here.

## 6. Sequential approval chain

Approvers are asked one level at a time (manager, procurement, security, finance, CFO) by email with approve and reject links. No answer triggers reminders, then expiry. Every step is written to the audit log.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pa_vendors (
  vendor_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name           TEXT NOT NULL,
  risk_level     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (risk_level IN ('low', 'medium', 'high', 'blocked')),
  approved       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  blocked_reason TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pa_departments (
  department    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  manager_email TEXT NOT NULL,
  annual_budget NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  spent         NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  committed     NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pa_requests (
  request_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  requester_email TEXT NOT NULL,
  department      TEXT NOT NULL,
  vendor_id       TEXT,
  vendor_name     TEXT,
  amount          NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  currency        TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_usd      NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  description     TEXT,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  risk_level      TEXT,
  required_levels JSONB,
  flags           JSONB,
  final_reason    TEXT,
  decided_by      TEXT,
  po_number       TEXT,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  finalized_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pa_requests_recent ON pa_requests (department, vendor_id, created_at);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pa_audit_log (
  id         BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  request_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  event      TEXT NOT NULL,
  actor      TEXT,
  detail     TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS pa_po_seq START 1;

-- Demo data: edit or replace with your own vendors and departments
INSERT INTO pa_vendors (vendor_id, name, risk_level, approved, blocked_reason) VALUES
  ('acme-office', 'Acme Office Supplies', 'low', TRUE, NULL),
  ('cloudco', 'CloudCo SaaS', 'medium', TRUE, NULL),
  ('shadyparts', 'ShadyParts Ltd', 'high', TRUE, NULL),
  ('sanctioned-inc', 'Sanctioned Vendor Inc', 'blocked', FALSE, 'failed sanctions screening')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
INSERT INTO pa_departments (department, manager_email, annual_budget, spent, committed, status) VALUES
  ('engineering', 'user@example.com', 500000, 100000, 20000, 'active'),
  ('marketing', 'user@example.com', 120000, 100000, 15000, 'active'),
  ('legal', 'user@example.com', 80000, 20000, 0, 'frozen')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
SELECT 'approvals_ready' AS status;

SELECT v.vendor_id, v.name AS vendor_name, v.risk_level, v.approved, v.blocked_reason,
       d.department, d.manager_email, d.annual_budget, d.spent, d.committed, d.status AS budget_status,
       COALESCE((SELECT SUM(r.amount_usd) FROM pa_requests r
                 WHERE r.department = $2::text AND r.vendor_id = $1::text AND r.status IN ('approved', 'pending')
                   AND r.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'), 0) AS recent_vendor_spend
FROM (SELECT 1) x
LEFT JOIN pa_vendors v ON v.vendor_id = $1::text
LEFT JOIN pa_departments d ON d.department = $2::text;

WITH r AS (
  UPDATE pa_requests SET
    status = $2::text,
    final_reason = $3::text,
    decided_by = $4::text,
    po_number = CASE WHEN $2::text = 'approved' THEN 'PO-' || to_char(NOW(), 'YYYY') || '-' || lpad(nextval('pa_po_seq')::text, 5, '0') END,
    finalized_at = NOW()
  WHERE request_id = $1::text AND status = 'pending'
  RETURNING request_id, status, po_number, final_reason, decided_by, department, amount_usd
), b AS (
  UPDATE pa_departments d SET committed = d.committed + r.amount_usd FROM r WHERE d.department = r.department AND r.status = 'approved' RETURNING 1
), a AS (
  INSERT INTO pa_audit_log (request_id, event, actor, detail) SELECT r.request_id, 'finalized:' || r.status, r.decided_by, r.final_reason FROM r RETURNING 1
)
SELECT request_id, status, po_number, final_reason, decided_by FROM r;
INSERT INTO pa_audit_log (request_id, event, actor, detail) VALUES ($1::text, $2::text, $3::text, $4::text) RETURNING id;

## 3. Policy: spend, department & vendor risk

Loads the vendor and department budget, then applies spend tiers, 30-day vendor spend (anti order-splitting), budget limits, vendor risk and self-approval rules to decide the approval path.
